title: Rule
description: Front matter of a rule definition in the rules repo: the rule envelope every rule shares (docs/design: Initial System Design, Decisions: rule language), plus a title and a lifecycle status. The body is the rule itself; for an llm rule, natural language an LLM judge applies to a change. Scope fields left out match everything. A boundary rule (kind boundary) protects a boundary between repos: instead of judging a change, it names a condition on a run's scope, and a scope that meets it needs an architect before planning (ADR 0018). An approval rule (kind approval) names files a person must approve: a change touching a file in its scope waits for the rule's owner (ADR 0021).

id.description: Rule id, stable across the rule's versions, for example GO-ERR-1.

title.description: What the rule asks for, in one line.

scope.description: Where the rule applies: a change is in scope when its repo matches and at least one changed file matches both languages and paths.

org.description: Organization name, or * for every organization.

projects.description: Project names, or * for every project in the organization.

repos.description: Repo names, or * for every repo in scope (bounded to the rule's project for project-level rules, ADR 0025).

languages.description: Languages of the changed files, for example go or yaml.

paths.description: Slash-separated glob patterns relative to the repo root; ** matches any number of directories.

severity.description: hard blocks a change; soft warns.

owner.description: The role or group that owns the rule and decides on changes to it, for example architects.

version.description: Version of the rule, from 1; a change to the rule's meaning increments it.

evaluator.description: What evaluates the rule: an OPA/Rego policy, an architecture test, an LLM judge (natural language), or condition: evaluated by HOTL's own code from the envelope, for boundary rules (the boundary condition) and approval rules (the scope).

status.description: Lifecycle state; active when left out. Shadow rules are evaluated and reported but never block.

kind.description: change (when left out): the rule judges a change. boundary: the rule protects a boundary between repos, and its boundary condition is checked against every run's scope before planning. approval: a change that touches a file in the rule's scope (repos and paths) needs the rule's owner to approve those files before it is pushed, such as an architect approving an ADR (ADR 0021).

level.description: Hierarchy level of the rule (ADR 0025): org applies to all projects in the organization; project applies only to the project(s) in scope.

overrides.description: Org-level soft rule ids that this project-level rule supersedes or suppresses (ADR 0025).

boundary.description: A boundary rule's condition: a scope meets it when every part given holds.

repos.description: The scope includes every one of these repos.

dependents.description: The scope includes at least atLeast repos that depend on one of the repos in of, by their approved repo profile's dependsOn.

atLeast.description: How many, from 1. A string, as front matter values are read as text.

newRepo.description: true: the scope proposes at least one new repo.

anyRepos.description: The scope includes at least one of these repos.
